extracted.intended_audience: attorneys who practice before the USPTO (trademark/non-patent), OED staff, and disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards governing imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO when a practitioner has been disciplined by a state authority, including notice, response/default, matching discipline, publication, and required post-discipline notifications and duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24; 35 U.S.C. § 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: Action taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline based on disciplinary action by a state authority under these statutes/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for discipline: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order predicates USPTO discipline on the respondent's state suspension (see Official Gazette notice language referencing violation of § 11.804(h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicate misconduct: state suspension for conversion of client funds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Georgia Supreme Court suspended Ms. Saunders for twelve months for conversion of client funds for her own personal use, in violation of Rules 1.15(I)(c) and 1.15(II)(b) of the Georgia Rules of Professional Conduct found in Bar Rule 4-102(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State findings of misconduct (here, conversion of client funds) form the factual predicate for reciprocal discipline at the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching discipline: identical to state-imposed discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline imposed by the USPTO should be identical to the discipline imposed by the state (here: suspension for twelve (12) months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO order imposes the same term and type of discipline as the state authority's decision unless circumstances warrant otherwise under the governing regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and service: certified mail and requirement to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' was sent by certified mail notifying Respondent of the Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline; Respondent received the Notice and Order but did not file a response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service (certified mail, with receipt) and providing an opportunity to respond are procedural prerequisites; the respondent may file a response contesting reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond (§ 11.24(d)): no genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is determined there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and suspension is the appropriate discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the respondent does not timely contest, the OED Director (or delegated authority) may treat the state discipline as conclusive for purposes of imposing reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement: Official Gazette notice content
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the provided 'Notice of Suspension' wording identifying the respondent, the USPTO practice area affected, the disciplinary action and its predicate, and references to the statutory/regulatory authority and FOIA reading room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must state the respondent's name, authorization (e.g., authorized to practice trademark/non-patent matters), the suspension term, the basis/predicate state ruling (including citation and misconduct), and where disciplinary decisions are publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-discipline duties: comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 contains the practitioner's duties upon suspension (e.g., notification to clients, return of papers and property); compliance with these duties is required following imposition of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO must notify other relevant state disciplinary bodies, courts, and the public about the imposed discipline and its reasons as part of reciprocal discipline procedures.
